title: Recognizing the Second Correction
hook: Correction #2 creates the zone. BOS #3 still has to activate it.

launchpad.outcome: Tell Correction #2 from Correction #1, find the zone-forming candle inside it, and explain why a potential zone without BOS #3 is not a trade.
launchpad.missionQuestion: Which correction creates the zone, and which candle inside it?

takeaways: Correction #2 is the pullback after BOS #2. Correction #1 comes after BOS #1.
Correction #2 creates the zone: its last bearish candle (demand) or last bullish candle (supply) before BOS #3.
Don’t mark the whole correction as the zone.
Until BOS #3 occurs, the zone is only potential.

slides.headline: Correction #2 is where the zone begins.
slides.line: Two pullbacks, two very different jobs. Here you learn to tell them apart and find the one candle that matters.

slides.headline: Correction #1 or Correction #2?
slides.line: The order of the breaks tells you which correction you’re looking at.

versus.label: Correction #1
points: Comes right after BOS (break of structure) #1.
Preferably pulls back toward the 15M break.

versus.label: Correction #2
points: Its last opposite-colour candle before BOS #3 forms the zone.

slides.headline: Find the second pullback.
slides.line: Bullish example. BOS #1, Correction #1 and BOS #2 are marked.
slides.why: That candle is part of the second pullback, the one after BOS #2.

after.caption: Correction #2 comes after BOS #2. This is the correction that creates the zone.

slides.headline: One candle creates the zone.
slides.line: Bearish example. In a supply setup, the zone comes from the last bullish candle of Correction #2.
slides.ask: Tap the candle that creates the supply zone.
slides.why: That’s the last bullish candle of Correction #2, the one right before sellers take over.

after.caption: The supply zone is drawn from that one candle. It’s a potential zone until BOS #3.

slides.headline: Don’t box the whole correction.
slides.line: Correction #2 creates the zone, but the zone is one candle, not the whole pullback.

check.prompt: Correction #2 has four candles. What do you mark as the zone?

options.label: The whole of Correction #2
options.feedback: Don’t mark the entire correction as the zone. Find the last opposite-colour candle of Correction #2.

options.label: Its last opposite-colour candle before BOS #3
options.why: Right. For demand it’s the last bearish candle. For supply it’s the last bullish candle.

slides.kicker: Step 5 · A zone that never activates
slides.headline: A potential zone isn’t a trade.
slides.line: Bullish example. Correction #2 forms a zone. Watch what happens next.

steps.caption: Correction #2 creates a potential demand zone from its last bearish candle.
No BOS #3. No 5M candle closes above the high Correction #2 pulled back from. The zone never activates.

check.prompt: Price keeps trading in this potential zone. Is that a trade?

options.label: Yes, price is back in the demand zone
options.feedback: The zone was never activated. BOS #3 must occur before the retest-entry model applies.

options.label: No, BOS #3 never happened
options.why: Right. Correction #2 created a potential zone, but without BOS #3 it never becomes active. No trade.

slides.quote: Correction #2 creates the zone. BOS #3 decides if it counts.

slides.prompt: In your own words, how do you tell Correction #2 from Correction #1, and which candle forms the zone?
slides.modelAnswer: Correction #1 comes right after BOS #1, and Correction #2 comes after BOS #2. Correction #2 creates the zone. For demand, the zone is the last bearish candle of Correction #2 before BOS #3. For supply, it’s the last bullish candle. I don’t mark the whole correction, and the zone stays potential until BOS #3 occurs.
